common_name: Berry Bomb Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Director Jacobs Frosty Red Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Berry Bomb is Bailey Nurseries' Chick Charms-series trade name for Sempervivum 'Director Jacobs', a van der Steen selection valued for its cupped, cilia-fringed red leaves that give the tight 3-4 inch rosette a frosted appearance; color deepens toward purple-black as the rosette closes up in winter cold. Plant offsets on the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, where bright light intensifies the red pigment that fades in shade. It offsets freely on short stolons, forming a dense mat within a season or two, and like all sempervivums resents wet feet far more than cold — sharp drainage matters more than soil fertility.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Gold Rush Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Lemon-to-Cherry Open-Form Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of very well-drained, gritty soil in full to partial sun in spring or fall.

directions: Gold Rush is a Chick Charms-series selection (plant patent applied for) with an open rosette of narrow, pointed leaves that opens lemon-yellow in spring and deepens to cherry-red tones through summer and fall, a more dramatic seasonal color swing than the related Gold Nugget. Press offsets onto very well-drained, gritty soil in full to partial sun; strong light is needed to trigger the red flush. It spreads readily on stolons to form a loose colony 5-6 inches across, and like other sempervivums needs protection from standing water and heavy winter rain rather than from cold.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Blushing Garnet Hens and Chicks (Colorockz Series Olive-to-Fiery-Red Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, gravelly, sharply drained soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Blushing Garnet is a Gielis-bred selection in the Colorockz series, opening olive-green and developing fiery yellow-and-red overtones when grown in strong outdoor sun; in shade or indoors it stays mostly green. Plant offsets in lean, gravelly, sharply drained soil in full sun and expect a tight, compact 3-4 inch rosette that offsets regularly into a neat clump. As with other sempervivums, hardiness to well below 0F is not the limiting factor — wet winter soil and standing water are what kill it.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Pink Pearl Hens and Chicks (Zonneveld Calcareum Blue-Green to Pink Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of well-drained, ideally slightly alkaline gritty soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Pink Pearl is a Zonneveld-named selection of Sempervivum calcareum, the lime-loving houseleek species known for unusually good tolerance of cold, wet winters compared to most sempervivums. Its blue-green rosettes flush pink to burgundy at the leaf tips in full summer sun, an effect that fades in shade. Press offsets onto well-drained, ideally slightly alkaline gritty soil in full sun; it offsets generously on stolons to form a spreading 5-6 inch clump. Give it the sharp drainage all houseleeks need, but it is more forgiving of a damp winter than most cultivars in the genus.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Spaghetti Marinara Hens and Chicks (Vaughn Narrow Velvety Red-and-Tan Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of very well-drained, lean gravelly soil in full to partial sun in spring or fall.

directions: Spaghetti Marinara is a Vaughn hybrid (Sempervivum 'Space Dog' crossed with itself, with S. montanum, S. grandiflorum, and S. marmoreum in its background) grown for narrow, velvety red-and-tan leaves that resemble strands of pasta in sauce, shifting toward copper and orange through the seasons. Plant offsets in very well-drained, lean gravelly soil in full to partial sun; the rosette stays under 3 inches across and spreads readily on stolons to carpet crevices and rock garden pockets. Short pink flower stalks appear on mature rosettes before they die back, leaving offsets to carry on the clump.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Slabber's Seedling Hens and Chicks (Pink-and-Olive Mat-Forming Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Slabber's Seedling combines pink and olive-green in a single 3-4 inch rosette, offsetting rapidly on stolons to knit together into a neat, weed-suppressing mat, making it a useful filler cultivar for trough and crevice plantings. Press offsets onto lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun for the tightest form and best color; it is extremely cold-hardy but, like all sempervivums, needs protection from standing water and heavy winter rain rather than from frost.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Irene Hens and Chicks (Heuffelii Burgundy-Hearted Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant offsets in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun in spring or fall; water only when the soil is fully dry.

directions: Irene is a Sempervivum heuffelii selection with a burgundy-red rosette centered by a light yellow-green heart and fine white leaf margins, turning deep purple in winter. Heuffelii types differ from typical Sempervivum tectorum hybrids by offsetting from within the mother rosette rather than on long stolons, giving a tighter, more clustered clump. Grow in full sun in very well-drained, lean soil and water only when the soil is fully dry during the growing season — heuffelii selections are notably more drought-tolerant, and more prone to winter rot in wet soil, than most other houseleeks. Individual rosettes flower and die after several years, but the clustered offsets carry the clump on indefinitely.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide
North American Rock Garden Society — Sempervivum heuffelii culture notes

common_name: Hedgehog Hens and Chicks (MacPherson Spiky Green-and-Burgundy Roller Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun to light shade in spring or fall.

directions: Hedgehog is a MacPherson selection of Sempervivum globiferum subsp. hirtum, the 'roller' hens-and-chicks group known for chicks that detach on thin stolons and roll away to root independently rather than staying attached to the mother rosette. Its bright green, burgundy-tipped leaves are long, spiky, and tightly incurved, forming one of the larger rosettes among the roller-type sempervivums. Plant offsets in full sun to light shade in lean, sharply drained gravelly soil; it produces offsets abundantly and tolerates hard winter cold well, but like other sempervivums needs protection from standing water and heavy rain.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Giant Copper Canyon Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Large Copper-Red Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of very well-drained, gritty soil in full to partial sun in spring or fall, allowing room for a large mature rosette.

directions: Giant Copper Canyon is an outsized Chick Charms-series selection (plant patent pending) that forms a copper-red rosette exceeding 8 inches across, greening up in shade and intensifying to deep copper-red in strong sun. Plant offsets in very well-drained, gritty soil in full to partial sun, allowing plenty of room for the rosette to reach full size; it offsets on stolons to form an impressively large clump over a few seasons. Sharp drainage remains essential through winter, since this cultivar tolerates hard cold far better than wet soil.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Centennial Hens and Chicks (Bronow Large Magenta Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall, allowing room for a large mature rosette.

directions: Centennial is a Bronow selection that forms an unusually large rosette, exceeding 8 inches across, in vivid magenta that shifts toward green in cooler or shadier conditions and produces pink flowers on mature rosettes. Plant offsets in full sun in lean, sharply drained gravelly soil to maximize both size and color; it offsets regularly on stolons and builds into an impressive clump within a couple of seasons. As with all sempervivums, winter wet is the main hazard, not winter cold.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide
